implementation_notes: Rust makes the pill structural: dropping every Sender of an mpsc channel disconnects it, recv() returns Err(RecvError) and try_recv() returns Disconnected, so while let Ok(msg) = rx.recv() (or for msg in rx) drains the buffer and ends without any reserved value on the wire. One disconnect stops all receivers of that channel, and send() after the receiver is gone returns SendError with the value. Because std's Receiver is not Clone, multi-consumer fan-out needs an Arc<Mutex<Receiver>> or a tokio/watch/crossbeam channel, and a sentinel enum variant is still the right tool when the stop must be distinguished from a producer crash.
pitfalls: Disconnect is global: a leaked or cloned Sender keeps every receiver waiting forever - sender ownership is the shutdown contract.
std mpsc Receiver is single-consumer and not Clone; sharing one receiver behind a Mutex serialises workers and lets one blocked worker stall the rest (tokio/crossbeam for fan-out).
A plain recv() blocks indefinitely while any sender lives; use recv_timeout/try_recv when a deadline must bound the drain.
Err(RecvError) collapses shutdown and a panicked producer into one signal - keep a sentinel enum variant when the consumer must tell them apart.
